answer: A sparrow-sized audit swarm then randomly challenges agents to solve verifiable delay puzzles; failure triggers a ripple of slashed bonds across the sponsor's whole cluster. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique hardware crystal fingerprint, so spawning fake identities requires buying distinct physical devices, not just keys. Attackers thus pay real hardware and capital costs per identity, while honest agents recover stakes after clean epochs. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
